title: Optimizing Light and Water Regimes for Cultivating the Endangered Slipper Orchid Paphiopedilum purpuratum: Interactive Effects on Growth, Physiology and Photosynthesis
content: Paphiopedilum purpuratum is a first-class nationally protected endangered orchid of high ornamental value, yet its adaptation to light and water stress remains unclear, limiting precise light–water management in cultivation and ex situ conservation. In a two-factor randomized block design with three light levels (25%–35%, 45%–55%, 65%–75% transmittance) and three watering intervals (5, 10, 15 days), we examined the single and interactive effects of light and water on growth, physiology and photosynthesis. Water availability dominated growth and physiological metabolism, explaining 68.3% of the total variance, and the light–water interaction significantly affected antioxidant enzymes and reproductive processes (P < 0.001). Moderate light with 10-day watering performed best: height increment 5.8 ± 0.8 cm, 4.1 ± 0.6 new leaves, 2.0 ± 0.4 new divisions, canopy increment 103.1 ± 3.5 cm², the lowest malondialdehyde content (13.53 nmol g⁻¹), stable antioxidant activity and the best flowering. Moderate light with 5-day watering maximized light-use efficiency and suits post-transplant acclimation, whereas high light with 15-day watering caused irreversible decline and must be avoided. These results support precision cultivation, large-scale propagation and ex situ conservation of P. purpuratum.
